clauses.reason: Retirement coverage is an independent legal extension; broader 1942 statutory coverage and exclusions are disclosed earlier functional changes, not a named 8083 ending under the owner rule. Personal accrued rights are separately preserved.

The replacement appointment and status rule, including denial of removal protection, remains amended until parent ending under the owner strike-and-insert ruling. EO 9830 replaces the rules and expressly revokes 8083 and 7915 on its global effective date.

The supersession of 3375 is a legal change effective May 1, 1939, not an unperformed future task. Formal revocation ends 8083 authority without reviving 3375 or undoing historical effects; May 1, 1939 is commencement, not expiration.

research_rationale:
EO 8083 independently extends retirement coverage, replaces Rule II section 3(d), and supersedes EO 3375, all effective May 1, 1939. Complete official page 1577 and EO 9830 Parts I–III were read; images of original page 1 and actor pages 1,4,5,11 were inspected. EO 9830 names 8083 without exception in Part III, under the opening global effective date May 1, 1947. January 24, 1942 statutory coverage revision and EO 9154 exclusions are earlier functional replacement candidates, disclosed under the owner ruling on unnamed instruments, not earlier formal ends of this named order. Wartime recruitment and 1946 transitional rules do not erase all earlier status rights. Historical supersession, completed appointments and accrued retirement or status rights are distinguished from continuing commands of revoked 8083.

savings.reason: Accrued retirement and competitive status rights, completed appointments and the completed supersession are distinguished from continuing 8083 authority. EO 9154 section 3 explicitly protects retirement rights acquired before its May 1, 1942 issuance despite January 24 retroactivity; the 1942 Act section 10 preserves rights of persons separated before its effective date. EO 9691 section 9 saves acquired reemployment rights. EO 9830 Part II recognizes competitive status and provides successor authority, but has no general clause continuing 8083 as an order. No individual pension payment or current right is inferred.
